messages:
sarah: FYI spike of 503s starting ~03:12 UTC for hosted inference. only affects requests routed to model reloads (hot-reload path). customers A/B reported auth failures & timeouts.

oncall-bot: Alert: service.redwood.api.gateway latency > 5s and upstream_5xx_rate > 4% (3 hosts). Incident ID: INC-2719.

sarah: digging into gateway logs now. sample upstream error: 
`UpstreamError: connection reset by peer (signal 11)`

alex: which cluster/region? any common model or quant variant?

sarah: region: us-west-2, pool: hosted-gpu-pool-7. model: redwood-small-quantized:v2 (hot-swap during canary rollout). payloads were long-context (85k tokens) for a few requests.

mike: hmm, hotmodel swap + quantized checkpoint restore + long context = risky. do you have the worker container logs?

sarah: pasted tail of runner logs (abridged):
```
[2024-05-10T03:12:14Z] loader: restoring quant checkpoint: shard-7
[2024-05-10T03:12:14Z] infer-runner: Allocating GPU mem for KV cache: 10.2G
[2024-05-10T03:12:15Z] infer-runner: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
[2024-05-10T03:12:15Z] kubelet: Killing container with id docker://runner-xyz: OOMKilled
```

emily-support: multiple paying customers hit 503s and are complaining about timeouts + billing. ETA for mitigation?

alex: immediate mitigation: switch routing for the affected model to the stable, non-quant variant and mark hot-reload disabled for that model group. I can kick that now.

alex: (runs) `infractl routing set --model redwood-small-quantized:v2 --fallback redwood-small:v1 --drain 60s`

infra-bot: Routing change applied to pool hosted-gpu-pool-7. Traffic shift to fallback model started (10% -> 100% over 60s).

sarah: after routing change, gateway 5xxs dropped to baseline within 90s. customers reporting fewer errors.

mike: still need root cause. logs imply OOM during checkpoint restore, but segfault suggests possible device driver or loader bug when mapping quant tensors + KV cache. can you collect node dmesg + coredump?

sarah: grabbed dmesg snippet: 
```
[  123.456789] Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (infer-runner) total-vm:7543212kB, anon-rss:10240000kB
[  123.456790] oom_reaper: reaped process 23456 (infer-runner), now anon-rss:0kB
[  123.456800] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

mike: NVRM GPU fallen off bus is worrying. could be hardware transient, but coincides perfectly with quant restore path. please upload core + nvcrash logs to /tmp/incident-2719/. also run `nvidia-smi -q` on node to capture driver state.

sarah: uploaded artifacts: /tmp/incident-2719/{core.23456, nvcrash-20240510.tar.gz, worker.log}. Also ran quick repro script hitting the endpoint with a long prompt while triggering a model swap header. got consistent crash locally (dev repro).

mike: thanks. I'll reproduce in my lab GPU. if it's reproducible, we need a code patch to make the loader defensive when restoring quantized shards (guard allocations, fallback to CPU page mapping) + a short-term policy to disable hot-reload for quantized models.

emily-support: can we get a proactive customer comms note? I'll draft a short status: "We've mitigated by routing impacted traffic to a stable model; engineering is investigating root cause. We will provide updates in 2h."

alex: created a short-lived feature flag: `disable_hot_reload_for_quant_models=true` and applied to us-west-2. command: `infractl featureflags set --env us-west-2 --flag disable_hot_reload_for_quant_models --value true`

infra-bot: Feature flag applied. Canary nodes: 4/4 healthy.

mike: reproduction in lab shows loader calling cuMemAlloc with size slightly under reported available memory, then a kernel fault in tensor map when sequence length + kv cache pushes usage over cliff. Patch idea: pre-reserve a safety margin before restore and fallback to CPU for large KV allocations. I'll open PR and cut a canary runtime build.

sarah: PR would be great. until then, is the fallback routing stable enough for customer-facing services? we still have a few in-flight requests but errors are low.

mike: yes fallback is good. we'll also schedule a rolling restart of the affected worker pool to clear any lingering bad device state. schedule in 15m.

oncall-bot: Action: rolling-restart initiated on hosted-gpu-pool-7 (2024-05-10T03:29:40Z). Expected duration: 6m.

sarah: rolling restart completed, no further 5xx spikes. closing immediate customer escalation. moving to follow-up & postmortem channel.

alex: follow-up items: (1) disable hot-reload for quantized models by default, (2) add safety-reserve in loader, (3) improve observability for memory headroom during model restore, (4) customer comms template.

mike: opening incident PR with repro steps, attached core backtrace and suggested patch. tagging for priority in next runtime sprint.

emily-support: thanks team — will send customers the update and credit impacted requests per SLA. :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks everyone. moving thread to #postmortems/INC-2719 now.
